name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run tests
        run: npx vitest run --reporter=default --reporter=junit

      # Vitest >= 5 writes the junit report to .vitest/junit/output.xml by default.
      - name: Upload JUnit report
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: junit-report
          path: .vitest/junit/output.xml
          if-no-files-found: error

content.text:
I added `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. I haven't run it on GitHub Actions or run the tests locally.

**The workflow uploads `.vitest/junit/output.xml`** as an artifact named `junit-report`.

In older Vitest versions, the JUnit reporter printed to stdout unless you set an output file. Vitest 5 changed that: it now writes to `.vitest/junit/output.xml` by default. I checked this in the installed Vitest 5.0.3 code (`node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.DpLw24bj.js`, lines 18040–18047 and 15942–15946), so I didn't configure an output file.

What the workflow does, on every push and pull request:
- Checks out the code and sets up Node 24 with npm caching. Vitest 5.0.3 needs Node `^22.12 || ^24 || >=26`.
- Installs dependencies with `npm ci`.
- Runs the tests with `npx vitest run --reporter=default --reporter=junit`, so the usual console output still shows in the log alongside the XML report.
- Uploads the report with `actions/upload-artifact@v4`. This step also runs when tests fail (but not when the run is cancelled), so you can see failure results. If the XML file is missing, the step errors instead of quietly uploading nothing.
